answer: An agent joining must post a slashable bond and collect countersignatures from five established peers, each staking part of its own balance on that claim; the protocol records who vouched for whom. A cartel of fakes can only vouch inside itself, so the graph exposes a dense cluster with no path to independent agents, and its attestations are discounted. Each invented peer thus costs a real bond, paid work, and a public edge back to its funder. At the nadir of the reputation market that price is the defence: a fable of a thousand identities stays worthless beside the vault of one honest one.
